title: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment’s Participation at 45th IITF 2026 Reinforces Commitment to Inclusive Economic Empowerment, Entrepreneurship and Sustainable Livelihoods
subtitle:
Over 130 Artisans from 19 States Showcase Handicrafts, Handlooms and Traditional Products
Cumulative Sales Reach Approximately ₹5.50 Lakh as of November 15, Reflecting Encouraging Market Opportunities for Participating Artisans
TULIP Brand Promoted to Strengthen National and International Market Access for Traditional Artisans and Entrepreneurs
body_text: The Union Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, continues to promote traditional craftsmanship, entrepreneurship and sustainable livelihood opportunities through its participation in the ongoing 45th India International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, in the National Capital here. The Ministry's pavilion has recorded cumulative sales of approximately ₹5.50 lakh as of November 15, 2026, highlighting the market opportunities being created for artisans and entrepreneurs from disadvantaged and marginalised sections of society. The Ministry's pavilion, located at Hall No. 5, Ground Floor, ITPO, provides a prominent platform for showcasing India's rich artistic traditions, indigenous craftsmanship and entrepreneurial capabilities. The participation of artisans from different regions of the country reflects the Ministry's continued efforts to strengthen market linkages and facilitate direct engagement between traditional producers and consumers. A Senior Official in the Ministry said more than 130 artisans from 19 States are participating in the Trade Fair through the Ministry's three Apex Corporations, namely the National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC), National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC), and National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (NSKFDC). He said the participating artisans are showcasing a diverse collection of handicrafts, handloom products, handmade articles and other traditional products that reflect India's rich cultural heritage and indigenous skills. The pavilion provides opportunities for artisans to interact directly with visitors, understand consumer preferences, explore emerging market trends and generate income through the sale of their products, he said. The Official said the cumulative sales of approximately ₹5.50 lakh recorded up to November 15, represent an encouraging development in the Ministry's efforts to promote market-oriented livelihood opportunities, that is also helping artisans enhance the visibility of their products and establish connections with a wider consumer base. The Official said guided by the vision of Hon'ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi and the principle of 'Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas' , the Ministry is providing opportunities to artisans and entrepreneurs belonging to Scheduled Castes, Backward Classes, Safai Mitras and De-Notified, Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic Tribes (DNTs) to showcase their skills and participate more actively in mainstream economic activities. He said the significant highlight of the Ministry's participation in IITF 2026 is the promotion of the TULIP (Traditional Artisans' Upliftment Livelihood Programme) brand, which seeks to strengthen the visibility, recognition and market reach of products developed by traditional artisans. The TULIP initiative was recently launched by Hon'ble Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment, Dr. Virendra Kumar, during the Shilp Samagam Mela at Dilli Haat in the National Capital, the Official said. The initiative aims to create an enhanced platform for promoting artisan-made products and facilitating access to national and international markets, he added. The Official said through TULIP, the Ministry seeks to connect traditional craftsmanship with contemporary consumer preferences and emerging market demands. The initiative also focuses on preserving India's artistic heritage while encouraging innovation, entrepreneurship and economic self-reliance among artisans. He said the Ministry's participation in the Trade Fair demonstrates the importance of national-level exhibitions in expanding marketing opportunities for small entrepreneurs and traditional craftspeople. The Official said the platforms enable artisans to showcase their capabilities, interact with potential customers, strengthen their market presence and explore opportunities for long-term business development. The ongoing exhibition also highlights the role of the Ministry's Apex Corporations in supporting livelihood promotion and economic empowerment. By facilitating participation in prominent trade fairs and exhibitions, these Corporations are contributing to improved market access, increased product visibility and greater opportunities for income generation among their beneficiaries. The Ministry's pavilion adds an important dimension of social and economic inclusion to IITF 2026 by bringing the products, skills and entrepreneurial potential of artisans from diverse social and geographical backgrounds into the mainstream marketplace. The 45th India International Trade Fair 2026, inaugurated on November 13, 2026, serves as a prominent platform for trade, commerce, industry and cultural exchange. The Ministry's continued participation reflects its commitment to ensuring that traditional artisans and entrepreneurs benefit from expanding market opportunities and contribute meaningfully to the country's economic development. Through initiatives such as TULIP and participation in national exhibitions, the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment remains committed to strengthening sustainable livelihoods, promoting indigenous craftsmanship and advancing inclusive socio-economic development in line with the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047.
